The local release row records May 15, 1999 as the date attached to the CoroCoro Comic June 1999 issue insert source group.
The local row and Bulbapedia raw source identify the distribution note as a CoroCoro Comic June 1999 issue insert, not a booster, deck, Fan Club route, or standard set release.

Bulbapedia's Togepi promo reference distinguishes the Japanese print's Original Series layout from the English Wizards Promo / Neo-era presentation, so layout and language are identity rails, not decoration.
Togepi matters here because CoroCoro could use a small, soft, new-generation character to make the TCG feel like it was already leaning toward the next world before the English Neo memory took over.

Agents should preserve CoroCoro Comic June 1999 issue insert route, May 15 1999 date, source index 093, Togepi identity, Ken Sugimori source-reference credit, Japanese Original Series layout, and non-equivalence with English Wizards Promo 30, Neo Genesis, ANA, and other Togepi memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: CoroCoro June 1999 Togepi: a small egg-shaped bridge to Johto
narrative.why_it_matters: This Togepi is quiet in the way important early promos often are. It is not a trophy, not a Charizard, not a tournament receipt. It is CoroCoro handing children a soft little future: Togepi, Sugimori's readable character grammar, and the sense that the card game was already stretching beyond the first 151. The exact route matters because the English Wizards Promo and Neo memories are loud. The Japanese CoroCoro insert has its own assembly: May 1999 magazine timing, source index 093, Original Series layout, and a creature whose gentleness helped the next era arrive without feeling like a rupture.

narrative.human_title: Togepi 093: the soft future in the magazine
narrative.why_it_matters: Togepi is not loud, and that is the point. In this row it arrives through CoroCoro as a little egg-shaped promise that Pokémon was about to get wider, softer, and stranger. Sugimori's character clarity helps it feel official even before the English Neo-era memory gets loud. The agent has to slow down here: source index 093, Japanese CoroCoro June 1999 route, Original Series layout, and the Japanese face all matter before the familiar word Togepi starts pulling the card into the wrong drawer.
